key_insight: SAMA factorizes instruction-guided video editing into separate semantic anchoring and motion alignment components, enabling precise, localized semantic edits while preserving original motion — without relying on brittle external priors.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between making accurate semantic modifications and maintaining faithful temporal motion in instruction-guided video editing, overcoming robustness and generalization limits caused by dependence on external priors.
method: Factorized design: split the editing task into Semantic Anchoring (where and what to change) and Motion Alignment (how to keep motion consistent).
Semantic Anchoring: inject instruction-conditioned anchors into the model’s latent/spatio-temporal representation to localize and control semantic edits precisely.
Motion Alignment: align temporal dynamics (e.g., attention trajectories or flow-aware features) during editing to preserve original motion patterns without external structural priors.
impact: Enables more robust, generalizable instruction-guided video edits that maintain temporal coherence — useful for production tools, content creation, and downstream research on controllable generative video models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two parallel branches: Semantic Anchoring (local edit) and Motion Alignment (temporal consistency), merging into edited video output.
Before/after frame pairs emphasizing accurate semantic change with preserved motion (e.g., object appearance changed but motion trajectory unchanged).
Flow/attention visualization illustrating preserved motion fields or attention maps pre- and post-edit to show temporal alignment.
Bar/line chart comparing semantic accuracy vs motion fidelity for SAMA and baseline methods to highlight improved trade-off.
paper_title: SAMA: Factorized Semantic Anchoring and Motion Alignment for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
paper_authors: Xinyao Zhang, Wenkai Dong, Yuxin Song, Bo Fang, Qi Zhang
